summary: Bash script that reproducibly renders site-astro/scripts/og.html to PNG via chrome-devtools-cli. The script navigates to og.html via file:// URL, sets viewport to exactly 1200×630 via emulate --viewport, waits for document.fonts.ready (Google Fonts loading from og.html), captures screenshot to $TMPDIR/og.png, copies to site-astro/public/og.png, and verifies output dimensions with sips (confirms 1200×630). Requires chrome-devtools-cli running (automatic with coldstart init).

summary: Regenerates public/og.png (the 1200x630 social card) from scripts/og.html by driving chrome-devtools-cli. Two environment constraints are the reason this is a script and not a one-liner: chrome-devtools REFUSES to write outside its allowed workspace roots, so the capture goes to a TMPDIR path and is copied into the repo afterwards; and resize_page silently does not apply, so the viewport must be set with 'emulate --viewport'. Rewritten this session after the first version could ship a stale card silently: it combined 'set -e' with '|| true' on every chrome-devtools call and used a FIXED temp path, so a failed capture left the previous run's PNG in place, passed the -f existence guard, and copied an old card into the repo while reporting success — which is also why 'ran it twice, identical output' was not evidence of reproducibility. Now uses a PID-unique temp path removed up-front and on EXIT via trap, no '|| true' swallowing, and hard failure if the viewport is not 1200x630 or the captured PNG is not 1200x630. It also awaits document.fonts.ready, without which the serif headline silently renders in a fallback face.
